As we know,
$\frac{\sin A}{a}=\frac{\sin B}{b}=\frac{\sin C}{c}$ and $\sin A, \sin B and \sin C$ are in A P$.
So, $a, b, cwill also be in $AP
\begin{aligned}
\therefore 2 b & =a+c \\
\text{ and } \cos A & =\frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2 b c}=\frac{b^2+c^2-(2 b-c)^2}{2 b c} \\

questions.q: In $\triangle A B C$, if $3 a=b+c$, then value of $\cot \frac{B}{2} \cot \frac{C}{2}$ will be
questions.solution:
Given, $3 a=b+c\because \quad \cot \left(\frac{B}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{s(s-b)}{(s-a)(s-c)}}$ and $\quad \cot \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{s(s-c)}{(s-a)(s-b)}}\begin{aligned} \therefore \cot \left(\frac{B}{2}\right) \cdot \cot \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{s(s-b)}{(s-a)(s-c)}} \\ \quad \times \sqrt{\frac{s(s-c)}{(s-a)(s-b)}}\end{aligned}=\frac{s}{(s-a)}=\frac{2 s}{2 s-2 a}$
On putting $2 s=a+b+c$, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \cot \left(\frac{B}{2}\right) \cdot \cot \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)=\frac{a+b+c}{a+b+c-2 a} \\ \Rightarrow & \cot \left(\frac{B}{2}\right) \cdot \cot \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)=\frac{a+3 a}{a+3 a-2 a}=\frac{4 a}{2 a}=2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The $\triangle P Q R$ is inscribed in the circle $x^2+y^2=25$. If $Q$ and $R$ have coordinates $(3,4)$ and $(-4,3)$, respectively. Then, $\angle Q P R$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $O$ is the point on centre and $P$ is the point on circumference. Therefore, angle QOR is double the angle QPR. So, it is sufficient to find the angle $Q O R$.
Now, slope of $O Q, m_1=\frac{4-0}{3-0}=\frac{4}{3}$ Slope of $O R, m_2=\frac{3-0}{-4-0}=-\frac{3}{4}$ Again, $\quad m_1 m_2=-1$ Therefore, $\quad \angle Q O R=90^{{}^{\circ}}$ Which implies that $\angle Q P R=\frac{90^{{}^{\circ}}}{2}=45^{{}^{\circ}}$.

questions.q: If $k$ be the perimeter of the $\triangle A B C$, then $b \cos ^2 \frac{C}{2}+c \cos ^2 \frac{B}{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & b \cos ^2 \frac{C}{2}+c \cos ^2 \frac{B}{2} \\ & =\frac{b}{2}(1+\cos C)+\frac{c}{2}(1+\cos B) \\ & =\frac{b}{2}+\frac{c}{2}+\frac{1}{2}(b \cos C+c \cos B) \\ & =\frac{b}{2}+\frac{c}{2}+\frac{a}{2} \quad(\because a=b \cos C+c \cos B) \\ & =\frac{a+b+c}{2}=\frac{k}{2}\end{aligned}$

By sine rule
$\begin{array}{ll} & \frac{a}{\sin P}=\frac{b}{\sin Q}=\frac{c}{\sin R}=k \\ \text{ Also, } & \frac{1}{2} a p_1=\Delta \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{2 \Delta}{a}=p_1 \\ \Rightarrow & p_1=\frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin P} \end{array}$ Similarly, $p_1=\frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin Q}$ and $p_3=\frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin R}$ Since, $\sin P, \sin Q, \sin R$ are in AP. $\therefore \quad \frac{1}{\sin P} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin Q}, \frac{1}{\sin R}$ are in $H P\Rightarrow \frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin P}, \frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin Q}, \frac{2 \Delta}{k \sin R}$ are in HP $\Rightarrow p_1, p_2, p_3$ are in HP.

questions.q: $A$ and $B$ are two points on one bank of a straight river and $C, D$ are two other points on the other bank of river, if direction from $A$ to $B$ is same as that from $C$ to $D$ and $A B=a, \angle C A D=\alpha, \angle D A B=\beta, \angle C B A=\gamma$, then $C D$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Clearly, $\angle C D A=\beta, \angle D C B=\gamma, \angle A C B_0=\pi-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$ Using since rule in $\triangle C A B$, we get
$\frac{A B}{\sin (\pi-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma))}=\frac{C A}{\sin \gamma}\Rightarrow C A=\frac{a \cdot \sin \gamma}{\sin (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)}$ Now, using sine rule in $\triangle C A D$, we get $\frac{C A}{\sin \beta}=\frac{C D}{\sin \alpha}\Rightarrow C D=\frac{C A \cdot \sin \alpha}{\sin \beta}=\frac{a \sin \alpha \cdot \sin \gamma}{\sin \beta \cdot \sin (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a $\triangle A B C$, if $\sin A \sin B=\frac{a b}{c^2}$, then the triangle is
questions.solution:
Given, $\sin A \sin B=\frac{a b}{c^2}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow c^2=\frac{a b}{\sin A \sin B}=\left(\frac{a}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{b}{\sin B}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow c^2=\left(\frac{c}{\sin C}\right)^2 \quad\left[\because \frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & \sin ^2 C & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & C & =90^{{}^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\triangle A B C$ is a right angled triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If in a $\triangle A B C, \sin ^2 A+\sin ^2 B+\sin ^2 C=2$, then the triangle is always:
questions.solution:
$\sin ^2 A+\sin ^2 B+\sin ^2 C=2= \frac{1-\cos 2 A}{2}+\frac{1-\cos 2 B}{2}+\frac{1-\cos 2 C}{2}=2\Rightarrow \cos 2 A+\cos 2 B+\cos 2 C=-1\Rightarrow 2 \cos (A+B) \cos (A-B)=-2 \cos ^2 C\Rightarrow 2 \cos (\pi-C) \cos (A-B)=-2 \cos ^2 C{[\because A+B+C=\pi] }\Rightarrow 2 \cos C[\cos C-\cos (A-B)]=0\Rightarrow -2 \cos C[\cos (A+B)+\cos (A-B)]=0\Rightarrow -\cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=0\Rightarrow \cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=0$
Therefore, one of them should be equal to zero.
So, exactly one angle is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

questions.q: The triangle $P Q R$ of which the angles $P, Q$, $R$ satisfy $\cos P=\frac{\sin Q}{2 \sin R}$ is
questions.solution:
Let sides of a triangle are $p, q, r$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Applying sine rule } \frac{p}{\sin P}=\frac{q}{\sin Q}=\frac{r}{\sin R}=\lambda \\
& \because \quad \cos P=\frac{\sin Q}{2 \sin R} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{q^2+r^2-p^2}{2 q r}=\frac{q}{2 r} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad q^2+r^2-p^2=q^2 \Rightarrow r^2=p^2 \Rightarrow r=p
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Triangle is isosceles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If an isosceles triangle of vertical angle $2 \theta$ is inscribed in a circle of radius $a$. Then, area of the triangle is maximum, when $\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $A D=a+a \cos 2 \theta \text{ and } B C=2 B D=2 a \sin 2 \theta\therefore$ Area of $\triangle A B C$ is given by $\Delta=\frac{1}{2} B C \times A D=\frac{2}{2} a^2(\sin 2 \theta+\sin 2 \theta \cos 2 \theta)\Rightarrow \quad \Delta=a^2 \sin 2 \theta+\frac{1}{2} a^2 \sin 4 \theta$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $\theta$, we get $\frac{d \Delta}{d \theta}=2 a^2 \cos 2 \theta+2 a^2 \cos 4 \theta$ For maximum or minimum, put $\frac{d \Delta}{d \theta}=0$. $\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & \cos 2 \theta & =-\cos 4 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & & 2 \theta & =\pi-4 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & & \theta & =\frac{\pi}{6}\end{array}$ Now, $\frac{d^2 \Delta}{d \theta^2}=-2 a^2 \sin 2 \theta \times 2-2 a^2 \sin 4 \theta \times 4=-4 a^2 \sin 2 \theta-8 a^2 \sin 4 \theta$ At $\quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{d^2 \Delta}{d \theta^2}=-4 a^2 \sin \frac{\pi}{3}-8 a^2 \sin \frac{2 \pi}{3}\begin{aligned} & =-4 a^2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-8 a^2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & =-6 a^2 \sqrt{3} < 0\end{aligned}$ Hence, $\Delta$ is maximum for $\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

questions.q: In an equilateral triangle, the in-radius, circum-radius and one of the ex-radii are in the ratio
questions.solution:
We have; $\Delta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2, s=\frac{3 a}{2}\therefore \quad r=\frac{\Delta}{S}=\frac{a}{2 \sqrt{3}}, R=\frac{a b c}{4 \Delta}=\frac{a^3}{\sqrt{3} \cdot a^2}=\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}$

Hence; $r: R: r_1=\frac{a}{2 \sqrt{3}}: \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}: \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot a=1: 2: 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle A B C$, if $a=30, b=24,c=18$, then $r_3$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given sides of a triangle are
$a=30, b=24, c=18\therefore \quad s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}=\frac{30+24+18}{2}=36$
Now, $\Delta=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{36(36-30)(36-24)(36-18)} \\ & =\sqrt{36 \times 6 \times 12 \times 18} \\ & =\sqrt{36 \times 36 \times 36}=216\end{aligned}\therefore \quad r_3=\frac{\Delta}{s-c}=\frac{216}{18}=12$
